roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is a premier offensive threat with Drought, enabling powerful coverage moves and setting the pace early. Securing this ace allows me to build a balanced roster around weather control and speed management. Spending the full 20 points ensures I have the strongest possible foundation for my team.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Prankster Tailwind provides essential speed control to complement Mega Charizard Y's Drought offense. Whimsicott's Grass/Fairy typing resists Water and Fighting threats while offering coverage against Dragon and Dark types. This creates a solid offensive core with built-in speed manipulation for the doubles format.

roster.name: Garchomp
roster.rationale: Garchomp provides essential Ground coverage to pressure Archaludon and Grimmsnarl, hitting both super effectively while resisting Electric and Poison threats. Its Dragon typing offers additional synergy by resisting Dragon moves and adding bulk to balance the frailty of Charizard Y and Whimsicott. This pick establishes a strong offensive core capable of handling the opponent's current roster.

roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar offers vital Fake Out and Intimidate support to protect the frail Mega Charizard Y and Whimsicott, while its Dark typing counters the opponent's Gholdengo and Mega Floette. At 18 points, it fits the budget and leaves enough points for 6 remaining picks to build a balanced team.

roster.name: Mega Lucario
roster.rationale: Mega Lucario provides essential Fighting coverage to pressure the opponent's Archaludon, Grimmsnarl, and Mega Floette, while its Steel typing resists Rock attacks threatening Charizard and Garchomp. At 11 points, it leaves sufficient budget for five cheap fillers to round out the roster. This pick maximizes offensive synergy with my existing Fire types and counters the opponent's core strategy.

roster.name: Krookodile
roster.rationale: Krookodile provides essential Ground/Dark typing to counter the opponent's Ghost and Steel types like Gholdengo and Archaludon, while its Intimidate ability synergizes well with Incineroar's support role. Its high Speed and access to Taunt help disrupt the opponent's setup strategies, filling a crucial offensive and utility gap in my roster.

roster.name: Stunfisk
roster.rationale: Stunfisk fills the critical Electric type gap in my roster while providing a Ground/Electric typing that resists Fire and Electric, complementing my existing Fire/Ground core. At only 1 point, it leaves me 4 points for my remaining 3 picks, ensuring I stay under budget while adding a defensive pivot with Static support.

roster.name: Steelix
roster.rationale: Steelix provides a massive defensive wall with 200 Defense to counter the opponent's Fairy/Dark core (Mega Floette, Grimmsnarl, Gardevoir) while resisting their key types. Its Steel/Ground typing complements my existing Ground types and offers a reliable pivot with Sturdy and Sheer Force. This pick leaves 2 points for a filler while securing a crucial defensive backbone.

roster.name: Manectric
roster.rationale: Manectric provides essential Electric coverage and speed (105 base) to complement my mid-speed core, helping pivot against Water/Ice threats the opponent might draft later. Its Lightning Rod ability also offers a defensive check to potential Electric moves from the opponent's setup sweepers. This fits the 1-point budget while addressing the lack of speed control and type diversity in my current roster.

roster.name: Avalugg
roster.rationale: Avalugg provides a crucial Ice type to my roster, offering coverage against Dragon and Ground types like Garchomp and opposing Dragons. Its high Defense stat complements my defensive backbone, and it resists Fire, which is a common offensive type in my team's matchups. This fills a type gap while staying within the 1-point budget.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Archaludon gives us a bulky Steel/Dragon core to weather Sun-led offenses from Mega Charizard Y and provide a reliable pivot. With flexible abilities (Stamina/Sturdy/Stalwart) we can adapt to the meta and complement a later speed control or breakers. This spend keeps options open for the rest of the roster while securing a top-tier defensive backbone.

roster.name: Grimmsnarl
roster.rationale: Grimmsnarl (16) adds reliable speed control and heavy support for Archaludon. With Prankster-enabled moves (screens, status), it helps your core stay safe and set up more comfortably while covering common Dragons and fairies.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo adds a fast, versatile Steel/Ghost pivot with Good as Gold, giving status immunity and reliable momentum. It complements Archaludon’s bulk and Grimmsnarl’s support by adding a durable win condition and strong matchup versatility. This 16-point pick fits the plan to round out a balanced roster without overlapping existing base species.

roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Adds a strong, fast special attacker to pair with Archaludon/Grimmsnarl/Gholdengo. Floette-Mega brings massive SpA/SpD with Fairy typing, pressuring Dragons and Dark-types and benefiting from Fairy Aura synergy with our backline.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult adds blazing speed and versatile offensive pressure, giving us a reliable breaker to punch through bulky cores. Its Dragon/Ghost typing provides valuable coverage while synergizing with Grimmsnarl's support and Archaludon's bulk. At 14 points, it fits the current budget and leaves flexibility for later picks.

roster.name: Rotom
roster.rationale: Rotom gives a versatile fast pivot to complement Archaludon, Grimmsnarl, and Dragapult, while providing immunity to Ground-type pressure that can threaten our Dragon/Steel core. Its Electric/Ghost typing covers Water and Ghost checks, and it can run Volt Switch or Willow/Wisp to keep momentum. It fits under the 11-point cap, leaving room for the remaining picks.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Forretress gives a low-cost hazard setter to wear down threats and add defensive utility for our bulkier cores. It pairs well with Archaludon, Grimmsnarl, Gholdengo, and Dragapult, while we preserve points for the remaining picks.

roster.name: Gardevoir
roster.rationale: Add a sturdy Fairy-type backline with strong STAB options that pair well with Grimmsnarl's Prankster support and Mega Floette. Gardevoir provides defensive presence and solid offensive pressure versus common threats while staying within the 10-point limit.

roster.name: Meganium
roster.rationale: Takes a 1-point pick that strengthens our defensive backbone with reliable utility. Meganium adds valuable support options (Reflect/Light Screen, Aromatherapy, Leech Seed) to back up Archaludon, Grimmsnarl, and Floette, while helping cover Water/Fire checks our roster lacks.
